hardware: Arc B570 10 GB; Ryzen 5 5600X; 128 GB RAM
engine_library_source: f8519b9; original gather_rows16, Gemm::f16 and swiglu_interleaved bodies unchanged
weights: Eight rotating random FP16 gate/up and down matrices; real N2560/F640 shapes, not streamed GGUF weights
method: 512 experts, ten unique expert IDs per token, grouped into the same source-row order for both paths.
Original bulk gather and full X/GU/H arrays versus per-expert gather and shared X/GU/H arrays; full Dm retained.
Every gathered half input, FP32 gate/up, FP16 SwiGLU result and FP32 down result is finite and bit-identical.
128-entry prefix/suffix guards on all compared and reused allocations pass.
Independent sampled FP64 GU/down checks use L1 bound1e-6; down reference uses the original half SwiGLU result.
Correctness-only copies capture all compact intermediates; these copies are omitted from both timings.
Warm both paths after the CPU oracle; three alternating rounds of two calls per path; medians reported.
No competing compilation or other GPU work; synthetic timings do not establish model prefill improvement.
notes: The three target arrays shrink from900MiB to90MiB at8192, excluding Dm, debug capture arrays and guards.
Per-expert gathers add launches. Every measured compact median is slower, with a small difference at8192.
Other GDN/attention buffers share the workspace, so this array-size reduction is not the whole-model VRAM reduction.
No production change is adopted on the basis of these synthetic timings alone.
